title: Abu Bakr
hook: his closest friend, companion in the cave, who believed him when others called it a lie

segments.voice: Yesterday, sahabi: a companion, anyone who met the Prophet as a believer and died a believer. Your line was the ones who were there. Whose lesson did you pass on? Day seven hundred ninety-nine.

Medina, the day the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, has died. The news is out, and the mosque is in uproar. Umar is on his feet, insisting it can't be true. Then a man rides in from his home at as-Sunh, on the edge of town. He doesn't speak to anyone. He goes straight into Aisha's room, uncovers the Prophet's face, and kisses him. Then he walks out to the crowd. Everyone is waiting to hear what the closest friend will say. His name is Abu Bakr.
screen: `THE MOSQUE IN UPROAR.` → `A MAN RIDES IN.` → `HE KISSES HIS FRIEND'S FACE.`

segments.voice: Bukhari records what he said. Whoever worshipped Muhammad: Muhammad has died. Whoever worships Allah: Allah is alive and does not die. Then he recited a verse from Surah Al Imran, in Pickthall's words: "Muhammad is but a messenger, messengers (the like of whom) have passed away before him." The report says it was as if people had never heard the verse until he recited it, and soon everyone was saying it. Umar said later that when he heard it, his legs gave way beneath him. So who was this man, steady enough to hold a whole city on that day? Earlier this year we heard the Prophet defend him in a quarrel, in Bukhari: when Allah sent me to you, you said, you are lying, and Abu Bakr said, he has told the truth, and he stood by me with himself and his wealth. Will you leave my companion alone? The tradition calls him as-Siddiq, the one who affirms the truth. And in another report, the Prophet said that if he were to take an intimate friend other than his Lord, it would be Abu Bakr. Then there is the cave. The Qur'an calls the Prophet the second of two, hiding with one companion, and commentators name that companion Abu Bakr. After the Prophet's death, the community chose Abu Bakr as caliph, to lead it. Sunni Muslims honor him as the first of the rightly guided caliphs. Shia Muslims hold that leadership belonged to Ali, and remember these days differently. The verse he recited is the same for both.
screen: `MUHAMMAD IS BUT A MESSENGER.` · `HE HAS TOLD THE TRUTH.` · `AS-SIDDIQ, WHO AFFIRMS THE TRUTH.` · `THE COMPANION IN THE CAVE.` · then, large: `THE SECOND OF TWO.`

segments.voice: The practice: be a loyal friend. Sit, and breathe. Think of a friend who is carrying something right now. A loss, a fear, a project nobody else believes in. Notice what loyalty would look like for them this week. Probably something small: a visit, a message that says I believe you, or simply showing up when others drift away. Choose one small thing. If you pray, you can ask Allah to make you a good companion to them. The bell holds the time.
Abu Bakr. The Prophet's close friend and companion in the cave, called as-Siddiq for affirming him when others called him a liar. Today's word.
Your line: the second of two. Today, be someone's second: the friend who stands beside them, says I believe you, and stays. Day seven hundred ninety-nine.

howItsDone: Muslims remember Abu Bakr as the Prophet's companion in the cave; Sunni Muslims honor him as the first caliph and call him as-Siddiq, while Shia Muslims view the succession after the Prophet differently.

what a scholar hears: as-Siddiq, the second of two in at-Tawbah 40, and the speech in Bukhari that ends with Al Imran 144.
